entities.summary: Heikki Ilmari Savolainen was a Finnish artistic gymnast. He competed in five consecutive Olympics from 1928 to 1952 and won at least one medal in each of them. In 1928, he won a bronze on pommel horse, which was the first-ever medal in gymnastics for Finland. Winning his last medal at the 1952 Summer Olympics in Helsinki, he became the oldest gymnastics medalist, at 44 years old; he delivered the Olympic Oath in the opening ceremony of the 1952 games. In 1932, Savolainen and his teammate Einari Teräsvirta had the same score on horizontal bar, but the Finnish team voted to give the silver medal to Savolainen.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Heikki Savolainen's Olympic achievements marked a significant moment for Finnish gymnastics and sports history, with his bronze medal in 1928 being the first-ever medal won by Finland. His participation in five consecutive Olympics from 1928 to 1952 also made him a notable figure in the sport.
